name: 东方故事IIv1.3b
group_note: ES2-lineage codebase (Taiwan, 1994-2000, Annihilator), Traditional Chinese. MAJOR encoding finding: the initial convert_lib.sh pass decoded this archive as GB18030, which -- being a superset covering nearly all byte sequences -- silently 'succeeded' on this BIG5-encoded content without ever erroring, producing complete mojibake (Bopomofo-range garbage, e.g. 'ㄏノ祅祘' for what BIG5 decodes as '使用者' 使用者注册程式') instead of a decode failure the pipeline could have caught. Re-ran the whole raw->work conversion with BIG5 instead (verified against the raw .c source with a quick Python decode trial across big5/gbk/gb18030/cp950 before committing to BIG5). Also needed: (1) master.lpc's connect(int port) switches on a hardcoded MUD_PORT (4000, the mudlib's original default) instead of this project's actually-assigned port (40144) -- every single connection was rejected regardless of WASM (driver log: 'Can not accept connection ... due to error in connect()'), fixed by updating the MUD_PORT macro; (2) master.lpc's valid_read/valid_write recursively load_object(SECURITY_D) with no re-entrancy guard -- textbook §7.1, caused 'Too deep recursion' on the very first security check, fixed with the documented re-entrancy-flag pattern; (3) adm/daemons/userid.lpc (identd/RFC1413 lookup, pure socket) gutted per §7.52; (4) is_chinese()'s classic GBK byte-pair check (strlen>=2 required) rejected single-character and odd-length slices under the Unicode codepoint model, blocking any 1 or 3-character Chinese name -- fixed to a CJK codepoint range check. Re-applied a previously-committed native fix (removing a #define MUD_NAME that collides with this driver's auto-predefined MUD_NAME, §7.39) that the BIG5 re-conversion had wiped out by regenerating work/ from raw/ -- checked git history for what else that commit touched before reapplying, only globals.h. Admin (fluffos/Mud@2026) seeded via real registration + a freshly-created adm/etc/wizlist (none shipped in the archive).
